prose: GeekWire reports Amazon's public beta of TorchNeuron, software that runs PyTorch code on Amazon's Trainium chips with no modification - previously, developers had to rework code to call Annapurna-specific interfaces, said Colin Brace, Amazon's VP of technology software. In private beta since late last year, TorchNeuron is Amazon's most direct attack yet on CUDA's lock-in: the pitch is that switching from Nvidia to Trainium becomes as simple as changing a setting. If it works at production scale, it removes the main practical objection to Amazon's price-performance play in AI chips.
highlights: Amazon opens TorchNeuron to all developers in public beta
Runs PyTorch code on Trainium chips unmodified
Previously required rewriting to Amazon-specific APIs
In private beta since late last year
Direct attack on CUDA lock-in: switching 'as simple as changing a setting'
